templates.title: Orchester team server
templates.description: The self-hosted Orchester team server and its admin, behind Caddy, for a public DNS name.
templates.note: From compose.yaml. Caddy publishes ports 80 and 443 and gets the certificate. After the deploy, the server's log shows the setup code; open https://<DNS name>/admin and enter it.
templates.stackFile:
# An Orchester team server with its admin, behind Caddy, for a host with a public DNS name (deploy/server/README.md).
# The images come from Docker Hub; no repository checkout is needed. Put the values into `.env` beside this file
# (from `.env.example`), then:
#   docker compose up -d
#   docker compose logs server     # the setup code, then open https://<ORCHESTER_HOST>/admin
# Caddy obtains and renews the public certificate (ports 80 and 443 must be reachable) and sends every request to the
# server, which serves plain HTTP on the private network and forwards every path outside /api to the admin. Only Caddy
# is published. No network or air gap: compose.private.yaml. A host that runs Traefik: compose.traefik.yaml.
#
# The private network has a fixed subnet so the server can trust Caddy's forwarded client address by its IP:
# `.2` Caddy, `.3` the server, `.4` the admin. If another network on the host already uses 172.29.0.0/24, set
# ORCHESTER_SUBNET_PREFIX.
services:
  server:
    image: ivanzaida/orchester-server:${ORCHESTER_VERSION:-latest}
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      ORCHESTER_SERVER_NAME: ${ORCHESTER_SERVER_NAME:-Orchester}
      # Caddy holds the public certificate; the server speaks plain HTTP on this network only.
      ORCHESTER_SERVER_TLS: "off"
      ORCHESTER_SERVER_ADDRESS: https://${ORCHESTER_HOST:?Set ORCHESTER_HOST to the server's DNS name}
      ORCHESTER_SERVER_TRUSTED_PROXIES: ${ORCHESTER_SUBNET_PREFIX:-172.29.0}.2
      ORCHESTER_SERVER_ADMIN_URL: http://${ORCHESTER_SUBNET_PREFIX:-172.29.0}.4:3100
      # The admin calls the API on the server's own address on this network; the port is never published.
      ORCHESTER_SERVER_ADMIN_API_LISTEN: ${ORCHESTER_SUBNET_PREFIX:-172.29.0}.3:8741
      # Caddy's certificate, for the key proofs apps check before entering a code: `auto` reads it and its renewals at
      # https://ORCHESTER_HOST; or set its SHA-256.
      ORCHESTER_SERVER_PROXY_CERTIFICATE: ${ORCHESTER_SERVER_PROXY_CERTIFICATE:-auto}
    # For `auto`: here ORCHESTER_HOST is Caddy, on this network.
    extra_hosts:
      - "${ORCHESTER_HOST:?Set ORCHESTER_HOST to the server's DNS name}:${ORCHESTER_SUBNET_PREFIX:-172.29.0}.2"
    volumes:
      - server_data:/data
    # GET /api/v1/server on the private listener, with bash alone (the image has no HTTP client).
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "bash", "-c", "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/${ORCHESTER_SUBNET_PREFIX:-172.29.0}.3/8741 && printf 'GET /api/v1/server HTTP/1.0\\r\\n\\r\\n' >&3 && read -r _ status _ <&3 && [ \"$$status\" = 200 ]"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    networks:
      backend:
        ipv4_address: ${ORCHESTER_SUBNET_PREFIX:-172.29.0}.3
  admin:
    image: ivanzaida/orchester-server-admin:${ORCHESTER_VERSION:-latest}
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      ORCHESTER_ADMIN_SERVER_URL: http://${ORCHESTER_SUBNET_PREFIX:-172.29.0}.3:8741
      # Signs the CSRF tokens and seals the admin's cookies: 32 random bytes in base64 (`openssl rand -base64 32`).
      ORCHESTER_ADMIN_SECRET: ${ORCHESTER_ADMIN_SECRET:?Set ORCHESTER_ADMIN_SECRET}
      # Orchester Cloud's public address, for signing in and linking through the browser and for invites by email.
      # Set it empty to use codes only.
      ORCHESTER_ADMIN_CLOUD_URL: ${ORCHESTER_ADMIN_CLOUD_URL-https://orchester-cloud.lurq.dev}
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "node", "-e", "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:3100/admin/https').then((r) => process.exit(r.ok ? 0 : 1), () => process.exit(1))"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    networks:
      backend:
        ipv4_address: ${ORCHESTER_SUBNET_PREFIX:-172.29.0}.4
  caddy:
    image: caddy:2
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
      # HTTP/3, which Caddy advertises on 443.
      - "443:443/udp"
    configs:
      - source: caddyfile
        target: /etc/caddy/Caddyfile
    volumes:
      - caddy_data:/data
      - caddy_config:/config
    networks:
      backend:
        ipv4_address: ${ORCHESTER_SUBNET_PREFIX:-172.29.0}.2
    depends_on:
      - server
configs:
  # Everything goes to the team server, which answers /api itself and forwards every other path to its admin. No
  # access log is turned on.
  caddyfile:
    content: |
      ${ORCHESTER_HOST:?Set ORCHESTER_HOST to the server's DNS name} {
          reverse_proxy ${ORCHESTER_SUBNET_PREFIX:-172.29.0}.3:8080
          header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000"
      }
networks:
  backend:
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: ${ORCHESTER_SUBNET_PREFIX:-172.29.0}.0/24
volumes:
  server_data:
  caddy_data:
  caddy_config:

templates.title: Orchester team server (private network)
templates.description: The Orchester team server and its admin with the server's own certificate on port 8740: no public DNS name, or air-gapped.
templates.note: From compose.private.yaml. Clear the Orchester Cloud address to use codes only. After the deploy, the server's log shows the setup code; open https://<host>:8740/admin and enter it.
templates.stackFile:
# An Orchester team server with its admin, for a host with no public DNS name: a private network, or an air-gapped one
# (deploy/server/README.md). The server presents its own certificate (tls = "self_signed") on port 8740 and forwards
# every path outside /api to the admin on the private network. The images come from Docker Hub, or from `docker load`
# without the internet. Put the values into `.env` beside this file (from `.env.example`), then:
#   docker compose -f compose.private.yaml up -d
#   docker compose -f compose.private.yaml logs server     # the setup code, then open https://<host>:8740/admin
services:
  server:
    image: ivanzaida/orchester-server:${ORCHESTER_VERSION:-latest}
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      ORCHESTER_SERVER_NAME: ${ORCHESTER_SERVER_NAME:-Orchester}
      # Names and addresses people reach this host by, for the generated certificate (comma-separated). Read only
      # when the certificate is generated, on the first start.
      ORCHESTER_SERVER_TLS_NAMES: ${ORCHESTER_SERVER_TLS_NAMES:-}
      ORCHESTER_SERVER_ADMIN_URL: http://admin:3100
      # The admin calls the API here, on the private network only; this port is never published. The server warns at
      # start that it listens on every interface of its container: that is this network, as long as 8741 stays
      # unpublished.
      ORCHESTER_SERVER_ADMIN_API_LISTEN: 0.0.0.0:8741
    ports:
      - "8740:8080"
    volumes:
      - server_data:/data
    # GET /api/v1/server on the private listener, with bash alone (the image has no HTTP client).
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "bash", "-c", "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/8741 && printf 'GET /api/v1/server HTTP/1.0\\r\\n\\r\\n' >&3 && read -r _ status _ <&3 && [ \"$$status\" = 200 ]"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    networks:
      - backend
  admin:
    image: ivanzaida/orchester-server-admin:${ORCHESTER_VERSION:-latest}
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      ORCHESTER_ADMIN_SERVER_URL: http://server:8741
      # Signs the CSRF tokens and seals the admin's cookies: 32 random bytes in base64 (`openssl rand -base64 32`).
      ORCHESTER_ADMIN_SECRET: ${ORCHESTER_ADMIN_SECRET:?Set ORCHESTER_ADMIN_SECRET}
      # Orchester Cloud's public address, for signing in and linking through the browser and for invites by email.
      # Set it empty on an air-gapped network: the admin then offers codes only.
      ORCHESTER_ADMIN_CLOUD_URL: ${ORCHESTER_ADMIN_CLOUD_URL-https://orchester-cloud.lurq.dev}
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "node", "-e", "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:3100/admin/https').then((r) => process.exit(r.ok ? 0 : 1), () => process.exit(1))"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    networks:
      - backend
networks:
  backend:
volumes:
  server_data:

templates.title: Orchester team server (Traefik)
templates.description: The Orchester team server and its admin behind the host's Traefik: no published ports.
templates.note: From compose.traefik.yaml. After the deploy, the server's log shows the setup code; open https://<DNS name>/admin and enter it.
templates.stackFile:
# An Orchester team server with its admin on a host that already runs Traefik (deploy/server/README.md, "Behind
# Traefik"). Nothing is published: Traefik holds the public certificate and reaches the server over its external
# network; the server serves plain HTTP there and forwards every path outside /api to the admin. Put the values into
# `.env` beside this file (from `.env.example`), then:
#   docker compose -f compose.traefik.yaml up -d
#   docker compose -f compose.traefik.yaml logs server     # the setup code, then open https://<ORCHESTER_HOST>/admin
#
# Only `server` joins Traefik's network. The admin and the server's private API listener stay on this stack's own
# network `backend` (fixed subnet: `.3` the server, `.4` the admin), which is internal, so no other container on
# Traefik's network reaches the listener that believes the admin's forwarded headers, even on a host that does not
# isolate Docker's networks from each other. The admin has no route out: invites by email are carried to Orchester
# Cloud by the inviter's browser instead of the admin's own server side. The server believes a forwarded client
# address only from Traefik's own address, TRAEFIK_ADDRESS.
services:
  server:
    image: ivanzaida/orchester-server:${ORCHESTER_VERSION:-latest}
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      ORCHESTER_SERVER_NAME: ${ORCHESTER_SERVER_NAME:-Orchester}
      # Traefik holds the public certificate; the server speaks plain HTTP to it.
      ORCHESTER_SERVER_TLS: "off"
      ORCHESTER_SERVER_ADDRESS: https://${ORCHESTER_HOST:?Set ORCHESTER_HOST to the server's DNS name}
      ORCHESTER_SERVER_TRUSTED_PROXIES: ${TRAEFIK_ADDRESS:?Set TRAEFIK_ADDRESS to Traefik's address on the Traefik network}
      ORCHESTER_SERVER_ADMIN_URL: http://${ORCHESTER_SUBNET_PREFIX:-172.29.0}.4:3100
      # The admin calls the API on the server's address on `backend` only; the port is never published.
      ORCHESTER_SERVER_ADMIN_API_LISTEN: ${ORCHESTER_SUBNET_PREFIX:-172.29.0}.3:8741
      # Traefik's certificate, for the key proofs apps check before entering a code: `auto` reads it and its renewals at
      # https://ORCHESTER_HOST, out through Traefik's network (the host must reach its own name); or set its SHA-256.
      ORCHESTER_SERVER_PROXY_CERTIFICATE: ${ORCHESTER_SERVER_PROXY_CERTIFICATE:-auto}
    volumes:
      - server_data:/data
    # GET /api/v1/server on the private listener, with bash alone (the image has no HTTP client).
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "bash", "-c", "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/${ORCHESTER_SUBNET_PREFIX:-172.29.0}.3/8741 && printf 'GET /api/v1/server HTTP/1.0\\r\\n\\r\\n' >&3 && read -r _ status _ <&3 && [ \"$$status\" = 200 ]"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    labels:
      traefik.enable: 'true'
      traefik.docker.network: ${TRAEFIK_NETWORK:-traefik}
      # Every path on the host goes to the server, as with Caddy: it answers /api itself and forwards the rest.
      traefik.http.routers.orchester-server.rule: Host(`${ORCHESTER_HOST:?Set ORCHESTER_HOST to the server's DNS name}`)
      traefik.http.routers.orchester-server.entrypoints: ${TRAEFIK_ENTRYPOINT:-websecure}
      traefik.http.routers.orchester-server.tls: 'true'
      traefik.http.routers.orchester-server.tls.certresolver: ${TRAEFIK_CERT_RESOLVER:-letsencrypt}
      traefik.http.routers.orchester-server.middlewares: orchester-server-hsts
      traefik.http.routers.orchester-server.service: orchester-server
      traefik.http.middlewares.orchester-server-hsts.headers.stsSeconds: '31536000'
      traefik.http.services.orchester-server.loadbalancer.server.port: '8080'
      # Plain HTTP on the host goes to HTTPS, as Caddy does.
      traefik.http.routers.orchester-server-http.rule: Host(`${ORCHESTER_HOST:?Set ORCHESTER_HOST to the server's DNS name}`)
      traefik.http.routers.orchester-server-http.entrypoints: ${TRAEFIK_HTTP_ENTRYPOINT:-web}
      traefik.http.routers.orchester-server-http.middlewares: orchester-server-https
      traefik.http.routers.orchester-server-http.service: orchester-server
      traefik.http.middlewares.orchester-server-https.redirectscheme.scheme: https
      traefik.http.middlewares.orchester-server-https.redirectscheme.permanent: 'true'
    networks:
      backend:
        ipv4_address: ${ORCHESTER_SUBNET_PREFIX:-172.29.0}.3
      traefik: {}
  admin:
    image: ivanzaida/orchester-server-admin:${ORCHESTER_VERSION:-latest}
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      ORCHESTER_ADMIN_SERVER_URL: http://${ORCHESTER_SUBNET_PREFIX:-172.29.0}.3:8741
      # Signs the CSRF tokens and seals the admin's cookies: 32 random bytes in base64 (`openssl rand -base64 32`).
      ORCHESTER_ADMIN_SECRET: ${ORCHESTER_ADMIN_SECRET:?Set ORCHESTER_ADMIN_SECRET}
      # Orchester Cloud's public address, for signing in and linking through the browser and for invites by email.
      # Set it empty to use codes only.
      ORCHESTER_ADMIN_CLOUD_URL: ${ORCHESTER_ADMIN_CLOUD_URL-https://orchester-cloud.lurq.dev}
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "node", "-e", "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:3100/admin/https').then((r) => process.exit(r.ok ? 0 : 1), () => process.exit(1))"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    labels:
      traefik.enable: 'false'
    networks:
      backend:
        ipv4_address: ${ORCHESTER_SUBNET_PREFIX:-172.29.0}.4
networks:
  backend:
    internal: true
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: ${ORCHESTER_SUBNET_PREFIX:-172.29.0}.0/24
  traefik:
    external: true
    name: ${TRAEFIK_NETWORK:-traefik}
volumes:
  server_data:
